AN05B023a/d: sensory drive and downstream partners

Setup

The same comparison as 05_an05b023bc.Rmd, 07_an05b023cd.Rmd and 10_an05b023ac.Rmd, on the a/d pair. Everything that draws or fetches lives in _an_pair.R, so the pages cannot drift apart: only the pair, and what is said about it, is local to this file.

This is the pair of odd members: neither sits on the WG3/WG4/LgLG1a/LgLG1b set the pheromone story is about. AN05B023a is driven by LgAG1, WG1 and LgLG2, AN05B023d by LgLG3 and WG2, and they share no large sensory input, so the FOCUS set for the an05b023ad case in _paths.R carries both sides of that.

rgl cannot initialise headless on this machine, so rgl.useNULL is set before anything that might pull it in.

options(rgl.useNULL = TRUE)   # must precede any library that pulls rgl in (nat)

suppressMessages({
  library(neuprintr); library(malecns); library(nat)
  options(malecns.dataset = "male-cns:v1.0")   # malecns helpers ignore MCNS_DATASET
  library(coconatfly); library(coconat)
  library(dplyr); library(tibble)
  library(ggplot2); library(ggrepel); library(scales); library(patchwork)
})

R_DIR <- "/Users/fkampf/Documents/pheromone.paper/analyses/an_investigation/R"

# AN_CASE may already be set to another case from an earlier 01-03 run in this
# session, so pin it rather than relying on the fallback in _paths.R.
Sys.setenv(AN_CASE = "an05b023ad")
source(file.path(R_DIR, "_paths.R"))
source(file.path(R_DIR, "_an_pair.R"))
neuprint_login(server = MCNS_SERVER, dataset = MCNS_DATASET)

PAIR <- TARGET_TYPES   # left of zero, right of zero
PAIR
## [1] "AN05B023a" "AN05B023d"

Annotation tables are expensive to fetch, so they are cached in the global environment for the session.

load_once <- function(name, expr, envir = .GlobalEnv) {
  # eval() here evaluates a quote()d expression written literally in this file -
  # it is a lazy-evaluation idiom for "only run this fetch if not already cached",
  # not a parser of external input.
  if (!exists(name, envir = envir, inherits = FALSE)) {
    assign(name, eval(expr), envir = envir)
  }
  get(name, envir = envir)
}
# No BANC here: this page is a maleCNS-only follow-up. For a BANC cross-check,
# copy the guarded fct / fba block from 04_SN_AN_connections.Rmd (lines 48-65) -
# reticulate::py_require("caveclient") has to run before python initialises.

mba <- load_once("mba", quote(mcns_body_annotations()))

The sensory pool

The same leg and wing gustatory bristle pool as the other pages: wider than the receptor-typed set on purpose, so the generic taste bristles act as a built-in negative control.

contact_pool <- sensory_pool(mba)

length(contact_pool)
## [1] 1067

Downstream output of each type

Partners in contact_pool are dropped here, leaving the genuinely downstream side; the sensory section below keeps exactly what this one discards.

l_output <- type_edges(paste0("/type:", PAIR[1]), "o", contact_pool)
r_output <- type_edges(paste0("/type:", PAIR[2]), "o", contact_pool)

setNames(c(sum(l_output$total), sum(r_output$total)), PAIR)
## AN05B023a AN05B023d 
##      5908     12460

a vs d: difference

AN05B023a and AN05B023d are two bodies each, one per side, and both types are GABAergic, so the raw weight totals are directly comparable and no per-cell scaling is needed. AN05B023d is the larger of the two on input: 8344 and 9387 input synapses against 7509 and 6552, which is what frac_diff guards against.

The two overall output totals printed above are the caveat to watch: if one type makes substantially more synapses than the other, every bar shifts in its direction. frac_diff is the guard — each partner’s share of that type’s own downstream output — so read it alongside diff before calling a partner specific to one of the pair.

out_diff <- diff_of(l_output, r_output)

out_diff |> select(type, total_l, total_r, diff, frac_diff)

The bars run bottom to top, most a-biased (negative) to most c-biased (positive). MIN_DIFF only controls readability — with every partner type on one axis the labels are unreadable — so the count of types it hides is printed rather than left implicit.

MIN_DIFF <- 20   # synapses; a type must differ by at least this to get a bar

shown <- out_diff |> filter(abs(diff) >= MIN_DIFF)
sprintf("%d of %d partner types shown; %d hidden below |diff| = %d",
        nrow(shown), nrow(out_diff), nrow(out_diff) - nrow(shown), MIN_DIFF)
## [1] "155 of 830 partner types shown; 675 hidden below |diff| = 20"

The right-hand panel puts the difference back on a scale: 300 synapses is the whole story on a partner that receives 800 inputs and a rounding error on one that receives 20,000. It is fetched only for the types that survive MIN_DIFF, which is what keeps it from being the slow all-partners call.

bars_out <- bars_downstream(shown, mba)

count(bars_out, grp)
bc_plot(bars_out,
        pair      = PAIR,
        lab_cols  = unname(DIMORPH_COLS[as.character(bars_out$grp)]),
        grp_cols  = DIMORPH_COLS,
        x_lab     = sprintf("bars: %s − %s    dots: synapses given by %s (left) and %s (right)",
                            PAIR[2], PAIR[1], PAIR[1], PAIR[2]),
        share_lab = "share of that type's input from the pair")

Output onto dimorphic partners

Which of the two sends more of its output to partners the dataset calls dimorphic or sex-specific. Computed on out_diff, the whole downstream table rather than the MIN_DIFF subset, because this is a property of each type’s entire output and thresholding first would drop the tail where an annotated class can hide.

frac_l / frac_r are shares of that type’s own total, so “more” here survives one of the two simply being the bigger neuron.

dimorph_out <- dimorph_output(out_diff, mba)

dimorph_out

Total share onto annotated partners, per type:

setNames(colSums(dimorph_out[dimorph_out$dimorphism != "not annotated",
                             c("frac_l", "frac_r")]), PAIR)
## AN05B023a AN05B023d 
## 0.1167908 0.1597913
dimorph_output_plot(dimorph_out, PAIR)

Read the bar lengths first — that is the answer to “which one” — and the segments only for which class carries it. Note that not annotated is the majority class in mba, so both bars are short by construction; the comparison is between them, not against 100%.

09_an05b023_dimorphic.Rmd puts these two bars next to b and c, and splits them by volume: in the brain AN05B023d gives 21.8% of its output to dimorphic partners against 6.9% for AN05B023a, and in the VNC the order reverses.

Sensory input to a and d

The mirror image of the plot above, on the types the downstream view excluded: the leg and wing gustatory bristles of contact_pool. Left end of each line is what that bristle type gives AN05B023a, right end what it gives AN05B023d, and the bar is still right minus left.

There is no MIN_DIFF here. The pool holds 27 types, few enough to show whole, and on the input side a type contributing nothing to one of the two is exactly the observation worth keeping visible.

This is the section that carries the pair: the two do not share a driver. WG1 and LgLG2 go to a, LgLG1b and WG3 go to c, and the FOCUS types are bold on the axis.

l_input <- type_edges(paste0("/type:", PAIR[1]), "i", contact_pool, sensory = TRUE)
r_input <- type_edges(paste0("/type:", PAIR[2]), "i", contact_pool, sensory = TRUE)

in_diff <- diff_of(l_input, r_input)

in_diff |> select(type, total_l, total_r, diff, frac_diff)

The second panel inverts too. Downstream it asked what share of the partner’s input comes from the pair; here it asks what share of the bristle type’s whole output lands on them.

No dimorphism colours on this one: every body in the pool is unannotated for dimorphism, so that scale would come out uniformly grey. subclass is what the pool does carry, so the fill is leg versus wing bristle.

The FOCUS types are picked out in bold rather than in WEB_PALETTE, which gives LgLG1a and LgLG1b the very pink and blue that already mean right and left in this plot. Types are named as the connectome names them, so no receptor-channel grouping is implied.

bars_in <- bars_sensory(in_diff, mba, contact_pool)

is_focus <- as.character(bars_in$type) %in% FOCUS

bc_plot(bars_in,
        pair      = PAIR,
        lab_cols  = ifelse(is_focus, DARK_FG, DARK_DIM),
        grp_cols  = SUBCLASS_COLS,
        x_lab     = sprintf("bars: %s − %s    dots: synapses onto %s (left) and %s (right)",
                            PAIR[2], PAIR[1], PAIR[1], PAIR[2]),
        share_lab = "share of that bristle type's output onto the pair",
        lab_face  = ifelse(is_focus, "bold", "plain"))
